value.text:
Nearly three blocks a game. No lineman in the league has ever worked at that rate.

Akiem Brock came to the Eagles in Y88, the season Dorren Skura arrived in Philadelphia, and he has been on that line for all 80 games since. He has been credited with 230 blocks, 2.9 a game, well clear of Jawill Perkins, the next best at the position. Four seasons is a short road to the Hall. Brock made every one of them count.

The rings came fast. The Eagles beat the Broncos 40-22 in Super Bowl CXLVII in Y88 and the Bengals 44-14 a year later. A 32-22 loss to the Texans in Y90 was the only miss, and in Y91 Philadelphia was back on top, beating the Raiders 38-23 in Super Bowl CL. Three rings, and like every lineman, no MVP or Player of the Year award to go with them.

He arrives in the Y91 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Akiem Brock, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Three interceptions. That is all that stands between Damar Hobbs and the league record.

Hobbs has spent his whole career in the New England secondary, and in 248 games he has picked off 39 passes, three behind Daren Teamer's mark of 42. He has made 2,717 tackles as well, close to eleven a game, so the ball hawk is also one of the surest tacklers at his position. There is not a sack or a forced fumble on his line. He plays the ball, and when the ball is caught he plays the man.

His ring came in Y81, when the Patriots outlasted the Packers 48-45 in Super Bowl CXL, a shootout that took 93 points to settle. There has been no individual award, only season after season of the same steady work.

He is still playing and still chasing the record. He arrives in the Y91 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Damar Hobbs, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Nine tackles behind Lloyd Queen, and still coming.

Quenton Fuller has spent his career on the Chargers front, and in 280 games he has made 1,355 tackles, close to five a game. Only Aqib McClain and Lloyd Queen have made more from the defensive line, and Queen's 1,364 is within reach. Fuller has added 15 sacks and 4 interceptions, but his work is done at the line of scrimmage. He takes on the block, finds the ball carrier and brings him down.

There has been no ring and no individual award along the way. There has been a lineman who keeps showing up, season after season, and a total that has climbed into the top three the position has ever seen.

He arrives in the Y91 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Quenton Fuller, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
3,132 tackles. Only K'Lavon Settle has ever made more.

Terron Stidham came into the league as Rookie of the Year and spent his whole career in the Baltimore secondary, 282 games for the Ravens before he retired after Y90. He made his tackles at a rate of about eleven a game and intercepted 34 passes. He was never credited with a sack or a forced fumble. He read the play, closed the distance and finished it, snap after snap, season after season.

He did it without a ring, and the only individual award on his line is the one he won as a rookie. What he left instead is the second deepest tackle total the league has seen, 53 short of Settle's 3,185.

He arrives in the Y91 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Terron Stidham, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Four Super Bowl rings on the Atlanta line.

Calais Ham arrived on the Falcons line in Y84. He has played 152 games and been credited with 306 blocks, more than two a game. Few linemen have done more with every snap.

The rings came one after another under Dorren Skura, in Y84, Y85, Y86 and Y87, the last of them at the end of a perfect 17-0 season and a 30-21 win in Super Bowl CXLVI. Ham was in front for all of it, without an MVP or a Player of the Year award, because linemen do not win those.

He arrives in the Y87 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Calais Ham, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
A Jets linebacker since Y76, and the middle of that defense has rarely moved without him.

Kalif Suh has played 298 games and made 980 tackles, with 17 interceptions, 24 sacks and 10 forced fumbles. That is a linebacker who does a little of everything: about three tackles a game, a takeaway when an offense gets careless, and pressure when the call comes to go get the quarterback.

He won three rings in New York, in Y77, Y80 and Y82, all on Dorren Skura's teams. When Skura left for Atlanta, Suh stayed, and he has kept the Jets defense steady ever since.

He arrives under the higher bar of Career Legacy 7,500, the second player inducted under it after Juwann Gilman. Kalif Suh, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Eight rings, and the best rushing seasons the record board has ever seen.

Ryland Maxwell came into the league with the Jets in Y80 and was Rookie of the Year, winning titles in Y80 and Y82. When Dorren Skura left for Atlanta after Y82, Maxwell went with him, and the Falcons won every season from Y83 through Y87. The Eagles traded Gerrit Ogbah for him before Y91, putting him back with Skura, and Philadelphia won Super Bowl CL.

In 225 games he has carried the ball 2,705 times for 20,717 yards and 297 touchdowns, and caught 137 passes for 1,029 yards and 40 more. He owns the single-game rushing record at 237 yards, the single-season touchdown record at 39 and the single-season yardage record at 2,670, set in Y87. Three Offensive Player of the Year awards and three Super Bowl MVPs say he saves his best for the biggest stage.

Ryland Maxwell, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
One tackle. That was all that separated Aqib McClain from the most tackles any defensive lineman had ever made, and he did not stay behind for long.

He spent his whole career on the San Francisco front from Y74, 291 games in one jersey, and he made 1,521 tackles, the most ever by a defensive lineman. That is better than five a game, the busiest rate among the great interior linemen, and Lloyd Queen's old mark of 1,364 is now well behind him. He added 9 sacks and 3 interceptions, but the sacks were never the point. He takes on the run, sheds the block and finishes the play.

He did it without a ring and without an individual award, season after season for the 49ers, and the total kept climbing anyway. The record is his.

He arrives in the Y88 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Aqib McClain, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Few linemen have ever been busier on a snap-for-snap basis than Jawill Perkins.

He played 139 games and was credited with 304 blocks, a shade under two and a quarter every time he lined up. Among the league's linemen only Akiem Brock has blocked at a higher rate. He never piled up the games of the iron men up front. He made the games he played count.

He has four rings to show for it, without a single MVP or Player of the Year award, because that is how the position works. The credit goes to the quarterback who stays clean and the back who finds the lane. Perkins is the reason the lane was there. Seattle wears him on its banner.

Four rings, 304 blocks, and one of the best rates the position has seen. Jawill Perkins, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
